text:
Let ƒ$(x) = (\sin (\tan ^{–1}x) + \sin (\cot ^{–1}x))^{2} – 1, |x| > 1$.

If $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dx}\left (\sin ^{-1}(f(x))\right )$ and $y\left (\sqrt{3}\right )=\frac{π}{6}$, 
then y($-\sqrt{3}$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given ƒ$(x) = (\sin (\tan ^{–1}x) + \sin (\cot ^{–1}x))^{2} – 1$

 $= (\sin (\tan ^{–1}x) + \sin (\frac{π}{2}$ $- \tan ^{–1}x))^{2} – 1$

 $= (\sin (\tan ^{–1}x) + \cos (\tan ^{–1}x))^{2} – 1$

$= \sin ^{2}(\tan ^{–1}x) + \cos ^{2}(\tan ^{–1}x) + 2\sin (\tan ^{–1}x)\cos (\tan ^{–1}x) + 1$

$= 1 + \sin (2\tan ^{–1}x) - 1$

$= \sin (2\tan ^{–1}x)$

Also given $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dx}\left (\sin ^{-1}(f(x))\right )$

 Integrating both sides we get

y = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (f(x)) + C$

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (2\tan ^{–1}x)) + C$

Given $y\left (\sqrt{3}\right )=\frac{π}{6}$ mean x = $\sqrt{3}$ and y = $\frac{π}{6}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{π}{6}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (2\tan ^{–1}\sqrt{3}$)) + C

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{π}{6}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (2\times\frac{π}{3}$)) + C

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{π}{6}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$) + C

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{π}{6}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{π}{3}$ + C

$\Rightarrow$ C = 0

Now y($-\sqrt{3}$) means when x = $-\sqrt{3}$ then find y.

y = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (2\tan ^{–1}x))$

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (2\tan ^{–1}(-\sqrt{3}$)))

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (-2\tan ^{–1}(\sqrt{3}$)))

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (\sin (-2\times\frac{π}{3}$))

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (-\sin (2\times\frac{π}{3}$))

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\sin ^{-1} (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$)

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $-\sin ^{-1} (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$)

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ -$\frac{π}{3}$

= -$\frac{π}{6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
Let two points be A(1, –1) and B(0, 2). If a point
P(x', y') be such that the area of $\Delta$PAB = 5 sq.
units and it lies on the line, 3x + y – 4$λ$ = 0,
then a value of $λ$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Point P(x', y') lies on the line 3x + y – 4$λ$ = 0

$\therefore$ 3x' + y' – 4$λ$ = 0

Area of $\Delta$PAB = 5

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & x^{'} & y^{'} \end{array}\right |$ = $\pm$ 5

$\Rightarrow$ [(–2x') – (y' – 2) – (x')] = $\pm$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ – 3x' – y' + 2 = $\pm$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ 2 - 4$λ$ = $\pm$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = -2 or $λ$ = 3

text:
The mean and the standard deviation (s.d.) of
10 observations are 20 and 2 respectively.
Each of these 10 observations is multiplied by
p and then reduced by q, where p $\neq$ 0 and
q $\neq$ 0. If the new mean and new s.d. become
half of their original values, then q is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let observations are
$x_{1}, x_{2}, ...., x_{10}$

Here mean = 20 and standard deviation(S.D) = 2

When each of these 10
observations is multiplied by p then new observations are
$px_{1}, px_{2}, ....., px_{10}$

and new mean = 20p and new standard deviation(S.D) = 2|p|

Now when Reduced by q then new observations are

$px_{1} - q, px_{2} - q, ....., px_{10} - q$

and new mean = 20p - q and new standard deviation(S.D) = 2|p|

Given 20p - q = $\frac{20}{2}$ = 10

and 2|p| = $\frac{2}{2}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ p = $\pm$ $\frac{1}{2}$

If p = $\frac{1}{2}$ then q = 0 (not possible as given q $\neq$ 0)

If p = - $\frac{1}{2}$ then q = -20

text:
Let y = y(x) be a solution of the differential
equation,

$\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx}+\sqrt{1-y^{2}}=0$, |x| < 1.

If $y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, then $y\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx}+\sqrt{1-y^{2}}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{\sqrt{1-y^{2}}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^{2}}}+\frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin ^{-1} y + \sin ^{-1} x = c$

Given that $y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

So when x = $\frac{1}{2}$ then y = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\sin ^{-1}$ $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ $+ \sin ^{-1}$ $\frac{1}{2}$ = c

$\Rightarrow$ c = $\frac{π}{3}$ + $\frac{π}{6}$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

So  $\sin ^{-1} y + \sin ^{-1} x =$ $\frac{π}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin ^{-1} y =$ $\frac{π}{2}$ $- \sin ^{-1} x$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin ^{-1} y = \cos ^{-1} x$

Now $y\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$ means x = $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and find y.

Putting x = $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\sin ^{-1} y = \cos ^{-1}$ $\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$ = $\frac{3π}{4}$

y (at x = $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$) = sin($\frac{3π}{4}$) = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
If the equation, $x^{2} + bx + 45 = 0 (b$ $\in$ R) has
conjugate complex roots and they satisfy
|z +1| = 2$\sqrt{10}$ , then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}$
 + bx = 45 = 0 (b $\in$ R)

has roots $α$ + i$β$, $α$ – i$β$

sum of roots = – b = 2$α$

product of roots = 45 = 
$α^{2}$
 + $β^{2}$

Let z = x + iy

$\therefore$ |x + iy +1| = 2$\sqrt{10}$

$|x+iy+1|^{2}=\left (2\sqrt{10}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(x + 1)^{2} + y^{2} = 40$

$\Rightarrow$ ($α$ $+ 1)^{2} +$ $β^{2}$ = 40

 [putting real part $α$ in place of x and imaginary part $β$ in place of y]

$\Rightarrow$ $α^{2}$ + 2$α$ + 1 + $β^{2}$ = 40

$\Rightarrow$ 45 + 2$α$ + 1 = 40

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = -3

$\therefore$ -b = 2$α$ = 2$\times$(-3) = -6

$\Rightarrow$ b = 6

By checking options we found $b^{2} – b = 30$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$C_{1}$ : $y^{2}$
 $= ax, C_{2}$ : $x^{2}$
 = ay (a > 0)

P : intersection point of $y^{2}$
 = ax and $x^{2}$
 = ay

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{4}$
 $= a^{2}$
 $y^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{4}$
 $= a^{2}ax$ 

$\Rightarrow$ x = a, y = a

$\therefore$ Point P : (a, a)

Line OP : y = x

$\Rightarrow$ Point Q = (b, b)

Area $\Delta$OQR = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\times b\times b$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ b = 1

As line x = b bisect the area between curve

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{a}\left (\sqrt{ax}-\frac{x^{2}}{a}\right )dx$ = $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (\sqrt{ax}-\frac{x^{2}}{a}\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{a}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\times \frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{x^{3}}{3a}\right ]_{0}^{a}$ = $\left [\sqrt{a}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\times \frac{2}{3}-\frac{x^{3}}{3a}\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{a^{2}}{3}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{a^{2}}{3}$ - 0 = $\frac{2\sqrt{a}}{3}-\frac{1}{3a}$ - 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{a^{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{a}=2\sqrt{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{3}+2=4a\sqrt{a}$

Squareing both sides, we get

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{6}+4a^{3}+4=16a^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{6}-12a^{3}+4=$ 0

 Hence $a$ satisfy $x^{6} – 12x^{3} + 4 = 0$.

text:
For which of the following ordered pairs ($μ$, $δ$),
the system of linear equations

x + 2y + 3z = 1

3x + 4y + 5z = $μ$

4x + 4y + 4z = $δ$

is inconsistent ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For inconsistent system we need

$\Delta$ = 0 and atleast one of $\Delta$x, $\Delta$y, $\Delta$z $\neq$ 0

$\therefore$ $\Delta$ = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 \end{array}\right |$ = 0

$\Delta_{x}$ = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ μ & 4 & 5 \\ δ & 4 & 4 \end{array}\right |$

= (-4) - 2($μ$ - 5$δ$) + 3(4$μ$ - 4$δ$)

$\Rightarrow$ 2$μ$ $\neq$ $δ$ + 2   ....(1)

Only ($μ$, $δ$) = (4, 3) does satisfy the equation (1).

If $\int \frac{\cos xdx}{\sin ^{3}x\left (1+\sin ^{6}x\right )^{2/3}}=f(x)\left (1+\sin ^{6}x\right )^{1/λ}+c$

where c is a constant of integration, then $λf\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given I =  $\int \frac{\cos xdx}{\sin ^{3}x\left (1+\sin ^{6}x\right )^{2/3}}$

Let sin x = t

$\Rightarrow$ cos xdx = dt

$\therefore$ I = $\int \frac{dt}{t^{3}(1+t^{6})^{2/3}}$

I = $\int \frac{dt}{t^{7}\left (\frac{1}{t6}+1\right )^{2/3}}$

Let $\frac{1}{t^{6}}+1$ $= z^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\frac{6}{t^{7}}dt=3z^{2}dz$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dt}{t^{7}}=\frac{z^{2}}{-2}dz$

So I = $-\int \frac{z^{2}dz}{2(z^{3})^{2/3}}$

I = $-\int \frac{dz}{2}$

I = $-\frac{z}{2}+C$

I = $-\frac{1}{2}\left (1+\frac{1}{t^{6}}\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$

I = $-\frac{1}{2}\left (1+\frac{1}{\sin ^{6}x}\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$

I = $-\frac{1}{2\sin ^{2}x}\left (\sin ^{6}x+1\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}+C$

$\therefore$ $λ$ = 3 and f(x) = $-\frac{1}{2}$cosec$^{2} x$

Then $λf\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ = 3 $\times$ $-\frac{1}{2}$cosec$^{2}$ $\frac{π}{3}$

= 3 $\times$ $-\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{4}{3}$ = -2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
Let ƒ(x) = xcos$^{–1}(–\sin |x|)$, $x\in \left [-\frac{π}{2},\frac{π}{2}\right ]$, then
which of the following is true?
options:
ƒ' is decreasing in $\left (-\frac{π}{2},0\right )$ and increasing
in $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$
ƒ is not differentiable at x = 0

ƒ' is increasing in $\left (-\frac{π}{2},0\right )$ and decreasing
in $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $\cos ^{-1}(-x) =$ $π$ $- \cos ^{-1}x$

$\therefore$ ƒ(x) = x($π$ $- \cos ^{–1}(\sin |x|))$

= x($π$ - $\frac{π}{2}$ $+ \sin ^{–1}(\sin |x|))$

= x($π$ - $\frac{π}{2}$ $+ \sin ^{–1}(\sin |x|))$

= x$\frac{π}{2}$ + x|x|

$\therefore$ f(x) = $\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x\frac{π}{2}-x^{2}, & x<0 \\ x\frac{π}{2}+x^{2}, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

Now f'(x) = $\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{π}{2}-2x, & x<0 \\ \frac{π}{2}+2x, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

and f''(x) = $\left \{\begin{array}{ll} -2, & x<0 \\ 2, & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$

$\therefore$ ƒ' is decreasing in $\left (-\frac{π}{2},0\right )$ and increasing
in $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
An urn contains 5 red marbles, 4 black marbles
and 3 white marbles. Then the number of ways
in which 4 marbles can be drawn so that at the
most three of them are red is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here 5 red marbles and 7 non red marbles are present.

No of ways 4 marbles  can be chosen where at most 3 red marbles can be present.

Case 1: When 3 red marbles present

No of ways $= ^{5}C_{3}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{1}$

Case 2: When 2 red marbles present

No of ways $= ^{5}C_{2}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{2}$

Case 3: When 1 red marble present

No of ways $= ^{5}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{3}$

Case 4: When 0 red marbles present

No of ways $= ^{5}C_{0}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{4}$

$\therefore$ Total number of ways

 $= ^{5}C_{3}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{1} + ^{5}C_{2}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{2} + ^{5}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{3} + ^{5}C_{0}$ $\times$ $^{7}C_{4}$

= 70 + 210 + 175 + 35

= 490
